name: fabflows
description: Routes work from an expensive lead model to tool-scoped workers (explorer and researcher on Haiku, editor and test-runner on Sonnet, refuter and investigator on Opus) and makes the lead re-verify their reports. using-fabflows is the session entrypoint and standing opt-in to fabflows:build, a deterministic loop in which an Opus builder implements a spec and a fresh reviewer returns ACCEPT or REWORK; brainstorming turns a rough idea into that spec. fabflows-setup points the repository at GitHub Issues, Jira or Linear in a committed .claude/fabflows.json, so specs live in tickets instead of docs/specs/. The ticket skill keeps the ticket current, and the ticket.js hook requires Refs and Spec trailers on commits and the key in the PR title, and at session start reminds Claude to close tickets, or ask before cancelling them, whose PR merged or closed outside the session. trace writes an audit trace report outside the repo: each merged change with its PR approvers, ticket, approved spec hash, Compliance section and flags such as no-ticket or self-approved. An ACTIVE guard hook asks before package installs and runners such as npx, denies them in workers (one exception: pypdf into a literal scratchpad --target with --isolated), and blocks commits and pushes to a default branch, destructive commands (including ones written into a Makefile, npm script or shell script) and credential-file reads and writes. It fails open: a bug degrades to no guard, never a blocked session.
